source.title: Identifying Equivalent Training Dynamics
source.authors: William T. Redman; J. Bello-Rivas; M. Fonoberova; Ryan Mohr; Y. Kevrekidis; Igor Mezić

record.tranche_reason: The study compares grokking and non-grokking Transformer training with Koopman spectra, a different measurement from the original grokking studies.
record.gate_note: Only the Transformer experiments concerning grokking and weight-norm constraints are included. The other optimizer, FCN, and CNN results do not bear on the claim. The paper also describes prior work on grokking; cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The grokking section reruns Omnigrok's code, hyperparameters unchanged, to get one grokking and one non-grokking Transformer. It then reports only its Koopman-spectrum comparison between them. The loss curves (Fig. 5A/B) are figure-only reproductions used to set up that comparison. The paper gives no accuracy values, no delay estimates and no dataset-size or norm sweep, and it draws no conclusion about whether grokking or its weight-norm dependence holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that Transformers which do and do not grok have non-conjugate early training dynamics, that constraining weight norm appears to give more stable dynamics, and that this may allow grokking to be anticipated.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses Koopman-spectrum comparisons of training trajectories, rather than reproducing the original grokking measurements. It uses modular arithmetic Transformers and compares constrained with unconstrained weight norm.
record.method_sensitivity: The constrained versus unconstrained weight-norm setting changes whether grokking is reported. The supplementary comparison using 200 constrained iterations still finds distinct Koopman spectra.

fits_no_version.finding: In the first 100 iterations, constrained-norm (non-grokking) Transformers have a complex-conjugate Koopman eigenvalue pair on the unit circle. Unconstrained (grokking) Transformers have one outside it. The difference persists with a 200-iteration constrained window.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early-training Koopman spectra distinguish modular-arithmetic Transformers that later grok from those that do not.

record.problems: The grokking trajectories are shown in figures without numeric accuracy values or reported quantitative delay estimates. The study does not sweep training-set size. Its evidence for the norm comparison is limited to modular-arithmetic Transformers and Koopman spectra; the authors note that the spectra are numerical approximations and that interpreting their distances remains challenging.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant results were left out. Results on optimizers, FCNs, and CNNs do not test the listed grokking versions.

untested.parts: No accuracy values, chance-to-perfect jump, delay length, or training-set-size dependence are reported.
Only a reproduction of Omnigrok's constant-norm constraint, with no quantitative result. No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep or lazy-to-rich analysis.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges V1' label for the constrained run is wrong: the constraint is a deliberate manipulation reproducing Omnigrok ([62]), not a setting where V1 predicts grokking. 'Supports V3' also rests only on qualitative figure reproduction of prior work with unchanged code, so no verdict is given. If the curator instead treats Fig. 5A/B as an independent T3 replication, the most it could carry is a weak, figure-only 'supports' for V3's weight-norm switch.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report the specified training/test accuracy values, chance-level test accuracy, or a sweep showing how the delay changes with training-set size.
It does not measure gradual formation of a generalizing circuit, removal of memorizing components, or circuit-based progress measures.
It tests weight-norm constraint on modular arithmetic only; it does not test non-algorithmic data, initialization scale, or a lazy-to-rich transition.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is studied.
The study does not test weight decay or another low-norm bias as an efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking below a threshold.
The study does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
The study does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax artifacts.

rows.subject: single hidden layer Transformer with unconstrained weight norm
rows.size_stated: single hidden layer, four attention heads
rows.operation_detail: Train on modular arithmetic without constraining weight norm.

conditions.value: 20 independent seeds; 10 perturbed initializations per seed

rows.measure: Train and test loss over training steps; delayed generalization (grokking)
rows.value: Figure-only loss trajectory; the text identifies this Transformer as undergoing grokking.
rows.note: The paper identifies the run as grokking, but does not give numeric loss values or the claimed train/test accuracy and dataset-size details.
rows.check: This is a selection/setup condition: a reproduction of Omnigrok's grokking run, chosen as the 'does grok' group for the Koopman comparison. It is figure-only loss, with no accuracy or delay values, so it should not carry a V1 or V3 verdict.

rows.subject: single hidden layer Transformer with constrained weight norm
rows.size_stated: single hidden layer, four attention heads
rows.operation_detail: Train on modular arithmetic with constrained weight norm.

conditions.value: 20 independent seeds; 10 perturbed initializations per seed

rows.measure: Train and test loss over training steps; presence of grokking
rows.value: Figure-only loss trajectory; the text states that no grokking is observed.
rows.note: The paper reports no grokking with the norm constraint. The statement that train and test accuracy rise at similar iterations is presented as prior-work context, not as a numeric result here.
rows.check: This is a selection/setup condition reproducing Omnigrok's constant-norm run as the 'does not grok' group. The 'absent' state wrongly treats a deliberate manipulation as a failure of V1. V1 does not say grokking occurs under a norm constraint. The constant-norm effect itself is presented as prior work ([62]).

rows.operation_detail: Compute Koopman eigenvalues from the first 100 training iterations.
rows.value: Distinct spectrum; a complex-conjugate pair lies outside the unit circle.
rows.note: The spectrum is a training-dynamics measurement, not a measure of circuit formation or delayed-generalization accuracy.
rows.check: Correctly unlinked. Koopman spectrum is the study's own method output.

rows.size_stated: single hidden layer, four attention heads
rows.operation_detail: Compute Koopman eigenvalues from 200 constrained-training iterations and compare with the unconstrained model's first 100 iterations.

rows.note: The authors report that this comparison has more similar, though not perfectly matching, training losses; the spectrum still differs.
